clue.text: Briefly, something to entice you into books?

definitions.text: Briefly, something to entice you into books?

parts.words: Briefly, something to entice you into books
parts.note: a short promotional paragraph on a book jacket exists to tempt readers into buying and reading

explanation.walkthrough: 'Into books' reads as being keen on reading, but it means drawing a browser into a particular volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A short piece of publisher's copy on a dust jacket is written to lure readers in.

clue.text: Child covered in terrible bruises rants and starts to cry

indicators.note: the child is wrapped up inside the jumbled letters that surround it
terrible signals that the letters of the two words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child, covered in awful bruises, shouts angrily and begins to cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the piece wrapped up; 'starts to cry' is the definition, not a first-letters signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve suddenly into weeping is to start crying; the idiom describes an abrupt outbreak of sobbing.

clue.text: Group of riders thrown?

parts.note: jockeys mounted on horses are said to be up, as in a racecard naming who is up
a set is a group of people

explanation.surface: A party of horsemen get unseated.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Group of riders' as a set of people who are up in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown by a shock means being disturbed or distressed, a common synonym.

clue.text: Change needed at the top, if doctor's going to flourish

indicators.note: the opening letter of the medical word is swapped for another one

parts.note: a surgeon is a kind of doctor; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Advice that the head of a medical practice must be replaced if it is to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change needed at the top' swaps the initial S of SURGEON; the B is not clued, the definition fixing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow and develop rapidly, like a plant putting out buds, is to flourish.

clue.text: End of story which is boring

parts.note: that can replace which as a relative pronoun
the contraction 's stands for is
something flat is dull and boring

explanation.surface: The conclusion of a tale that fails to excite.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic idioms closing a discussion: there is nothing more to be said.

clue.text: Part of something insubstantial

indicators.note: part of says the letters are taken from inside the following word

explanation.surface: A fragment of a thing that has no real substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy and lacking body is thin, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: After a dry start in this place, day will turn stormy: get prepared

parts.note: TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol
here means in this place

indicators.note: turning stormy suggests violent upheaval, so the letters of the word day are jumbled

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: after a dry start the day will become stormy, so be ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a weather forecast; 'After' and 'start' only say the opening pieces come first, and 'get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be poised and ready for immediate use is to be prepared, as a weapon held in readiness.

clue.text: Naval officer, one in marine environment? No way

parts.note: a seal is an animal that lives in the sea

explanation.surface: A navy man who works in a marine setting? Never!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine environment' points at the sea, but the 'one in' it is a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sea Lords are senior admirals on the board running the British Royal Navy.

clue.text: British Rail in a struggle to find lender

indicators.note: a struggle is a scuffle, so the letters thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: The old national railway, British Rail, fighting to find someone to lend it money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Rail' looks like the old railway company, but British gives only BR.
explanation.definitionFit: A person running a library lends books to its members, so is a lender in a jokey sense.

clue.text: Best known part of Brontë family drama

definitions.text: Best known part of Brontë family

clue.text: Check made by tutor during break

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.definitionFit: A check on behaviour is a curb or control, which is restraint.

clue.text: Be seen going round lake on morning stroll

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places one piece after the other
the word Be encircles the letter for lake

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.definitionFit: To walk at a slow leisurely pace is to stroll.

clue.text: Short period needed to secure the rope

parts.note: a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A brief interval required to fix the line in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' turns TERM into TER, which secures THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a cord or rope tying an animal to a post.

clue.text: War memorial constructed on path behind church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: constructed means put together, so the letters are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A war monument built beside a path at the back of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is an empty tomb honouring the war dead buried elsewhere, like the Whitehall monument.

clue.text: Queen isn't put out, squeezing into box for premiere

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are pressed inside the word for box

parts.note: to box is to fight

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: The Queen is not upset at being squashed into a theatre box for an opening performance.

explanation.definitionFit: The opening night of a play or show is its premiere, the first public performance.

clue.text: Supporter attending home match has left before the end — so childish

parts.note: in means at home
a fan supports a team

parts.note: a tie is a cup match

explanation.surface: A fan at a home game who leaves before the final whistle is behaving like a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attending' is only a link setting the supporter beside home; 'so' introduces the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is babyish or immature is infantile, a near synonym.

clue.text: Lucky swimmer sheltering in safe place close to shore

indicators.note: the fish shelters within the stronghold

parts.note: a fort is a fortified safe place
a tuna is a fish, a swimmer

indicators.note: close to means the end of the following word

explanation.surface: A fortunate fish finds refuge in a haven near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person, but it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blessed with good luck is being fortunate, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Ambition to run saloon?

explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is energetic motivation; and one operates a car by steering it on the road.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-' leaves TID from TIDDLY, and RE goes into it.

clue.text: Money is raised, kept in store

clue.text: Shortly arrived back at university, beginning to study, here?
